papers.title: A mechanical property evaluation of graded density Al-Si10-Mg lattice structures manufactured by selective laser melting
papers.first_author_affiliation: Additive Manufacturing & 3D Printing Research Group, Faculty of Engineering, University of Nottingham, Nottingham NG7 2RD, UK

corresponding_authors.name: Ian Maskery
corresponding_authors.affiliation: Additive Manufacturing & 3D Printing Research Group, Faculty of Engineering, University of Nottingham, Nottingham NG7 2RD, UK

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究了梯度密度晶格结构的力学性能，其方法可转移至髋关节植入物的刚度匹配设计，但未涉及生物医学验证。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address biomedical implant applications, lacks fatigue testing, and uses Al-Si10-Mg (not a standard biomedical alloy) so no osseointegration or biocompatibility evaluation.

summary_zh.motivation: 探索梯度密度晶格结构在刚度匹配和能量吸收方面的潜力
summary_zh.method: 通过SLM制造Al-Si10-Mg梯度晶格试样并进行准静态压缩测试
summary_zh.result: 梯度晶格结构实现了刚度梯度化，并提高了能量吸收能力
summary_zh.validation: 通过实验压缩测试验证力学性能，并与均匀晶格对比

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the mechanical performance of graded density lattice structures for potential stiffness tailoring applications.
summary_en.method: Selective laser melting was used to fabricate Al-Si10-Mg lattice samples with graded density, followed by quasi-static compression testing.
summary_en.result: Graded lattice structures exhibited tunable stiffness gradients and enhanced energy absorption compared to uniform lattices.
summary_en.validation: Mechanical validation was performed via compression experiments, with comparison to uniform lattice benchmarks.
